record.context_brief: Upper bounds on period from relevant poles
record.original_question: Given a periodic Herman ring H of period p for a meromorphic function, can one prove an upper bound on p in terms of the number h of H-relevant poles, complementing the known lower bounds? This is especially asked for meromorphic maps with finitely many poles and at least one omitted value, such as functions of the form E(z)/((z-z0)(z-z1)...(z-zp)) where E is an entire function omitting a finite point.

evidence.quote: Theorem 5.9. Let H be a p-periodic Herman ring of a function f, and let h be the number of H-relevant poles. Then p >= h(h+1)/2.

For a given Herman ring H, Theorem 5.9 provides a lower bound on the period of H in terms of the number of H-relevant poles. Is it possible to find an upper bound on the period of H? This question seems to be more relevant for meromorphic maps with finitely many poles and with an omitted value. Such a function is of the form f(z) = E(z)/((z-z0)(z-z1)...(z-zp)), p > 1 and z0, z1, . . . , zp in C where E is an entire function omitting a finite point.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f be a transcendental meromorphic function on the complex plane. A Herman ring of f is a periodic Fatou component H of f on which the first-return map f^p (where p is the period) is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of a round annulus. Let H be a p-periodic Herman ring with cycle H = H_0, H_1, ..., H_{p-1} (so f(H_i) = H_{i+1 mod p}). A pole z* of f is called H-relevant if z* is surrounded by some H_i in the sense that z* lies in the bounded component of the complement of the core curve of H_i. Let h denote the number of H-relevant poles.

It is known that p ≥ h(h+1)/2 in general (with the stronger bound p ≥ h(h+3)/2 in certain situations).

Question: Establish an upper bound on the period p in terms of h (and other natural data of f). The question is of particular interest for meromorphic maps having only finitely many poles and at least one omitted value, namely functions of the form
    f(z) = E(z) / ((z - z_0)(z - z_1) ... (z - z_p)),
where p ≥ 1, z_0, z_1, ..., z_p ∈ C are distinct, and E is an entire function omitting a finite value of C. Prove or disprove the existence of such an upper bound, and if it exists, give an explicit form.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem complementing known lower bounds (p ≥ h(h+1)/2 by Nayak–collaborators, published in Indian J. Pure Appl. Math., 2022). No published upper bound on the period of a Herman ring in terms of the number of relevant poles appears in the literature; the problem is explicitly listed as an open question in a recent (Dec 2025) survey on Herman rings.

status_evidence.title: On periods of Herman rings and relevant poles
status_evidence.snippet: A lower bound on the period p of a Herman ring H is found in terms of the number of H-relevant poles h: p ≥ h(h+1)/2.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bound on period is established; upper bound not addressed.
